initial.title: Designing against eval drift means setting a stop rule
initial.body:
If you are automating a recurring workflow, eval drift is not a theory problem. It is the question of how you will know the system is no longer matching the work it was built to handle. In a small business, that usually shows up in one of three places: customer replies, invoices, or lead handling. The AI may look fine on the sample you used to build it, then real messages, edge cases, or a process change start pulling it off course.

The practical decision is simple: define the workflow, the measurable outcome, and the stop rule before you automate. For example, if an assistant is classifying inbox messages, decide what “correct enough” means and what level of manual review means the system needs a reset. Any threshold here is a control, not a promise; if you have not agreed it in advance, you are just hoping the model stays polite. Hope is not a control system.

For owner-operators, the key point is human approval. If the workflow touches money movement or any other high-risk decision, the machine should not decide on its own. Design for alerts, review, and a clear handoff back to you when confidence drops or patterns change.

The next step is to write one sentence for the workflow: “If X changes, we pause automation and review Y.” That turns eval drift from an abstract AI concern into an operational boundary you can actually run.

selected_lessons.application: The task explicitly forbids a CTA ('CTA rule: None'). L01 guides the closing: end with a neutral practical observation or next-step note rather than a meeting prompt. The post should help the owner understand evaluation drift as a workflow decision without inviting them to book a diagnostic.

steps.instruction: Define evaluation drift as a practical, bounded workflow decision: the risk that an AI system's performance degrades over time as real data diverges from the training or test data it was built on. Frame it as a threshold decision an owner must make before deploying any AI automation—not a problem to solve after launch.

Explain one concrete example grounded in the persona: a workflow automation trained on a representative month of customer emails or invoices may perform well during build and pilot, but real customer language, edge cases, or business changes can cause accuracy to drop. Show this as a measurable control point (e.g., 'the system flags 5% of decisions for manual review; if that rises to 15%, something has drifted').

Connect eval drift to the owner's approval authority: human sign-off is mandatory for money movement and high-risk decisions. Eval drift design means building a system that alerts the owner when confidence drops or patterns change, not a system that silently fails or requires the owner to monitor logs.

Describe the diagnostic step: in the free 30-minute call, identify the workflow's measurable outcome (e.g., invoice accuracy, response latency, classification correctness) and agree on a drift threshold. This becomes part of the pilot scope and success measure, not a separate phase.

State the practical next step for the owner: before considering any AI automation, ask 'How will I know if this system stops working?' and 'What decision or control do I need to stay in charge?' Eval drift design ensures the owner has that control from day one, not as a retrofit.

Close with a neutral observation (per L01) that reinforces human authority: The best automation is one where you stay in control because you can see when it's drifting. This is a design choice, not an afterthought.

constraints_to_preserve.handling: Do not invent customers, deployments, observed results, ROI figures, or multi-person team. Use only self-built demos and Bareni services as described in C02 and C03. Present eval drift as a design discipline, not a customer case study.

Reinforce that human approval is mandatory for money movement and high-risk decisions. Frame eval drift design as a control structure that keeps the owner in charge, not as a system that removes human authority.

Preserve the frozen persona: plain-speaking technical expert, founder-to-founder tone, trust over enthusiasm. Use the approved identity (Bareni as a consulting practice built by the thesis author) and the bounded service model (diagnostic, pilot proposal, working MVP).

Use plain English throughout. Present eval drift as a workflow decision and diagnostic step, not as a complex algorithm or inaccessible concept. Keep the one example (invoice/email accuracy drifting) distinct from existing system descriptions and grounded in the 1-10-person business persona.

It does not assert any current Bareni capability, deployment or observed result, and the framing is permitted by the approved task. Nothing in approved evidence contradicts a general definition of drift.
ledger.use_guidance: Keep as an explanatory framing only. Present drift as a general concept and a decision the owner makes, without implying Bareni has drift monitoring, evaluation tooling or deployed systems; approved evidence records automated testing as planned, not working.

ledger.rationale: The two diagnostic questions are a permissible next step for the reader. The trailing assertion that 'eval drift design ensures the owner has that control from day one' is an unsupported guarantee-style claim about outcomes.
ledger.use_guidance: Keep the two questions as the practical next step. Remove or soften the 'ensures' guarantee: state it as the intended design goal of a bounded pilot rather than an assured outcome, since approved evidence supports no delivered drift-control capability.

evidence.quote: Informational posts use no CTA or one soft closing sentence.

ledger.rationale: A neutral closing observation reinforcing human authority is a permissible instruction for how to end the post; it makes no factual claim about Bareni capabilities, customers or results.
ledger.use_guidance: Keep as the closing line with no CTA, no invitation to book, discuss or continue the conversation, and no implied scarcity. Keep the wording restrained and free of hype terms.

selected_lessons.text: For informational marketing content, treat any invitation to book a diagnostic, discuss the situation, or continue the conversation as a CTA unless the task explicitly authorises one. End with a neutral practical observation or next-step note instead of a meeting prompt.

reasons.actionability: Gives a realistic, concrete next step to draft a specific stop-rule sentence before automating high-risk or recurring workflows.
reasons.factual_grounding: Makes no unsupported claims, benchmarks, or invented customer references, accurately reflecting Bareni's operational principles.
